text: when students die during a school-sponsored team-building activity, responsibility typically falls on the organizing coaches/school staff, the school administration, and potentially the resort operators for failing to exercise proper diligence and safety protocols. the people responsible for the team building activity should answer these questions: - was there a formal and robust pre-activity risk assessment conducted to identify all potential risks that may cause harm to participating students? this is very basic and if this was not done, it is already a good starting point to build a case involving school negligence. - for the risks identified, what mitigation measures were to taken to eliminate or minimize the risk? - are there weather contigencies and equipment inspections conducted prior to the team-building? - are there comprehensive health screenings performed to determine if the students are fit for the activities scheduled? - are students allowed to opt out of specific physical activites without penalties if they feel unsafe? - were safety briefings done at the start of the team building activity? - what is the ratio of the supervising staff to students? - is a trained first aid responder present? this is typically needed if the team building includes physical activities. - in the team building conducted in previouis years, was there an anonymous formal feedback system where students can report feeling unsafe or harassed during the activities? text: alam nyo bakit nakaka trigger yung statement nya? kasi if she had in fact undergone proper bls training, she should have been familiar with the sequence ng bls & the consequence of stopping the cpr. antee tinuro po sa bls about chest compression fraction (ccf) which is the amount of time spent giving high quality cpr. and this ccf plays a big role in the survival of the patient. high ccf = better chances of survival. low ccf = poorer chances of survival. at ano ba yung most common reason na mababa yung ccf? long interruptions in between cpr. kaya nga kahit during rhythm check, when we check if may pulse & spontaneous breathing na, it is recommended sa aha guideline ng bls to limit this interruption to not more than 10 seconds. you read that right, not more than 10 seconds. pero makikita nyo sa drone video na nung pina hinto nya yung pag cpr, parang naglakas pa sila ng ilang minute para malipat sa transport vehicle. kahit oa sabihin niyang malapit lang yung ambulance but based sa video it took more than 10 seconds. so yung pasyente pa yung nag adjust na mailapit sya sa transport vehicle para mabigyan daw ng paunang lunas which is cpr na pina tigil nung emergency responder. :face_with_rolling_eyes: or kung hindi kayang ilapit yung ambulance, wala palang wheeled stretcher yung ambulance nila para yung yung dalhin papunta sa patient? or kung wala talaga, then atleast nag bigay sya ng continuous cpr kahit nung naglalakad pa lng sila.

heightens the meaning of accountability and response-ability that is congruent with the truth that can truly liberate and transform our consciousness.
